CLASS NAME MISMATCH (flagging per PLAN.md's 'decompiler merged wrong content' guidance, but here it looks like the whole class was mis-labelled rather than just its companion statics): the init block does NOT decode a Vorbis comment header (that's vendor-string + tag=value user comments, all string reads) - it instead reads a fixed sequence of small bit-packed integers matching the real libvorbis **mapping header** layout almost exactly: 16-bit mapping_type (discarded), a 1-bit flag gating submap_count=read(4)+1 (else 1, into anInt3555), a 1-bit flag gating a channel-coupling read(8) (matches the spec's coupling-steps placeholder for this port, which appears to only support the trivial/no-coupling or single-step case), 2 reserved bits (discarded, matches spec's mandatory reserved=0 field), then if submap_count>1 a single read(4) into anInt3557 (spec loops this per output channel - consistent with this client's audio being mono, i.e. the loop body only ever executes once), and finally per-submap: an unused 8-bit 'time placeholder' (discarded, matches spec exactly) followed by an 8-bit floor number (anIntArray3556[i]) and 8-bit residue number (anIntArray3554[i]). Recommend treating anInt3555/anIntArray3556/anIntArray3554/anInt3557 as submapCount/floorNumbers/residueNumbers/channelMux respectively in any future field-rename pass, and possibly renaming the class itself to something like VorbisMappingHeader.
